# Review — secret-history-109-114 (§§109–114)

Reviewer: adversarial, two passes. `units.json` and `gloss.json` edited in place by script; `t`, word counts, `p` and `ln` untouched. Unit numbers are 0-based positions in `sentences`; word numbers are the packet indices. No modern translation was opened or recalled; the comparison text was the published parts (especially 100-104, 105-108, 087-092, 043-054, 007-023) and the shared glossary.

Checked by script before and after: every `t` equals the packet's romanized words in order (504 words, 66 units); every word has exactly one morph Ming bracket and it equals the packet gloss; `p: true` is on the first unit of §§109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114 only (U0, U8, U21, U39, U52, U62) and every `ln` is the section of its first word; each suffix lemma occurs in its word's surface form (only fault: word 94, fixed).

### Findings refused or left (pass 1), with the reason
- U1 i "the main frame of the doorway fell in": the drafter's own note says it is read from the Ming alone; the published §§105–108 render the same phrase as the frame of his tent falling in. Left, the uncertainty is stated.
- U9 kü: Ming 也 would suggest "also", but the glossary already holds kü "just, indeed" with the Ming 也 as the same emphatic force; i leaves it unrendered. Left.
- U11 i "they met": the subject of učiražu is unstated; i is defensible; only the note, which fixed the subject as Temüjin and Börte, was changed.
- U13 i "knew Temüjin": tanižu has no stated object; the note already says "recognising by night". Left.
- U19 i "the host halted": the subject of qonoba is not stated; the note says so and the alternative (the Merkid halted) is arguable. Left as the drafter's honest uncertainty.
- U22 i active "had snatched … and taken her" for the passive abtalai: the note states the passive is kept in l and the active given in i; the published 100-104 has the passive without an agent. Left.
- U25 i "to take in": loose but honest, the note explains the levirate sense. Left.
- U41 abura: the glossary already reads it ab- + -ura "in order to take" (Ming 取); I would read it as the verb abura- of aburaγsan in U20 (compare aburaja, "rescue"), but overturning a published entry is not mine to do. Left, listed as a doubt.
- U48: the hardest unit; the drafter's reading (Belgütei has the Merkid "of bone" shot with blunt arrows) is one of several, and the note says so. Left.
- U54 "by Heaven and Earth": the dative -a on γažar-a is the agent after the passive nemegdežü, the same construction as qojar-a nököčegdežü in U53, so the "by" is justified. Left.
- U55 "invoked before … Heaven": published nereidčü is plain "naming"; "invoked" is the drafter's declared reading of the Ming 被題着. Left.
- U56 ba "also" not shown in i: i is plain; l keeps it. Left.
- U29 qalqu: could be read with qalqa "shield", but the Ming gives 惹 "provoke" and the drafter says the stem is uncertain. Left.
- U44 morph for qād keeps "rulers" in the morph gloss while l and i now say "sovereigns": the glossary entry itself says "rulers". Left.
- U7 "few as they were" for čüġen: a stretch but čüġen bejesijen dutaγ̇an is declared odd in the note. Left.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json (re-read of units.json after pass 1, then every entry)

Counts: major 0 · moderate 5 · minor 5 · trivial 2 · total 12.

Whole-file checks (by script): the keys equal the 174 novel forms exactly, no extras, none missing; the final bracket of every entry equals the Ming gloss in novel-forms.json; every `__broaden__` value begins with the existing shared entry whole plus " · "; each entry's lemma equals the morph lemma in units.json (after the fixes). Every entry was read against its word(s), the unit text and the morph. Known forms were checked against this part's Ming glosses: nearly all differences are spelling variants of the same gloss and need no broadening; the two real gaps are below.

### Findings refused or left (pass 2), with the reason
- hačitu keeps "enmity, vengeance" (the known hači entry carries both and the published hači "enmity, vengeance, a feud"); the house word in l/i is enmity.
- qalqu keeps "provoking, meddling": it is a labelled guess on the Ming 惹.
- qaratu "-tu, an ending (uncertain)", boldaqu-ju, asaraγsaγ̇ar, oroγ̇uldaqun and similar entries keep their hedges: they name no grammar they cannot support.
- erüsčü / erüsbe keep "erü- + -s- (uncertain)" although the glossary has erüsün (erü- + -sün); the two analyses agree on the stem and both are hedged.
- The broadened entries already present (buγ̇ura, daγ̇arižu, eme, oro, qād) were checked: each is justified by this part's text and the Ming (地名, 撞着, 妻, 位子, 王子) and is in the form "old entry whole · new reading". Left.
- Known entries whose Ming differs only in spelling or punctuation (müren 河 行, -(n)e 行, ulus 百姓, etc.) were not broadened: the sense is covered.
- No invented modern forms found. Cross-references in the entries (daγ̇arižu, qočorba, ülüdgebe, abtalai, boldaba) all exist in the glossary or this part.

## Remaining doubts
- Unit 19: who halted at qonoba (Temüjin's party, as i has it, or the Merkid); the note says so.
- Unit 24: "in pursuit of Temüjin" is supplied (Temüžin-i has no verb of its own); the circling itself follows 100-104.
- Unit 49: the participle reading of qučilduγsad (the Merkid who had ringed Burqan) is firm on grammar and on 100-104, but the -du- sense and the Ming 相圍繞 "together" are soft.
- Unit 48 as a whole (Merkidai, ele jasutu, who shot whom, where the quotation starts); unit 29 qalqu; units 31 and 37 boldaqu-ju ("made a shield/fence"), units 30 and 35 kürtekü bolba.
- Units 27–37 Chilger's lament: that the speaker is Chilger himself throughout is read from Čilger bi; Γatar, Qunar, Qokir are the glossator's own parenthetical guesses.
- Unit 41 abura (ab- + -ura against abura- "rescue/fetch"), unit 42 whose tent (in-ü), unit 55 nereidčü ("invoked"), erüs- (-s-), hemtelbe, ülüdgebe, ülidgebe (-ge-).
- Unit 56 ere hačitu: "as men with a vengeance to take" is a loose rendering of the Ming 男子 讐報.
- Units 63–64 ičigin-žarγaγ "powder-skin" and usun-u buluγan "water-sable" are guesses from the Ming.

## New house renderings and name spellings
- Names in i: Barqujin (Shiratori Barγužin; the draft's "Barguzin" replaced), Yeke-Chiledü (the draft's "Jeke-"), Chilger-Bökö, Küchü, Buqura, Botoqan-Boqorji (as 105-108), Börte-Üjin, Lady Üjin (Qatun-Üžin), Qo'aqchin, Qa'atai-Darmala, Dair-Usun, Toqto'a Beki, Yesügei Ba'atur, Mother Etügen (the Earth); Qaldun-Burqan, printed reversed once, is "Burqan Qaldun" in i.
- qād: "sovereigns" in l and i (as 007-023, 074-079). hači/ösül: "enmity"; the Ming 報 verbs: "repay". qutuγ eġede: "door-frame of his fortune" (as 105-108). eġede: "door-frame" in l. -ber / -ġer / -jer: instrumental. hünesü-ġer keis-: "as ash is scraped off" (as 087-092). ebür / helige / oro hoγtorγou: "bosom / liver / place … empty / halved" (as 105-108). tedüi after a genitive: "no bigger than" (as 100-104 qarča-jin tedüi amin). buγaγ̇u "cangue", qorγosun "sheep-dropping", noyan unchanged.
